status: RESEARCH OUTPUT — pure transcription of repo docs; requires human review before seeding cropRegistry
purpose: Base agronomic registry fields (names, seasons, waterNeedMm, tempOpt, droughtSensitivity, soilSuitability, market mapping, confidence) for the 9 SPECIALIZED/GENERAL crops, transcribed from docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md, docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md, docs/market/data-source.md, docs/market/market-architecture.md and docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md. Irrigation parameters (kcStages, rootDepthM, depletionFraction) live in crops.agronomy.json and are NOT repeated here.

rules.transcriptionOnly: Every value in this file is literally written in a document inside this repository. Nothing is estimated, averaged, converted, rounded or inferred. Where a value is not written down the field is ABSENT and the omission is listed in `gaps`.
rules.noInventedAgronomy: No agronomic number, Hindi term or soil score was authored here. Prose descriptions were NEVER converted into numeric scores.
rules.publishedBlock: Each crop carries a `published` object holding the verbatim cells of the source table row, so a reviewer can check every transcription against docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md without opening the doc.
rules.sourceRefShape: { org, title, url, accessed, confidence, note }. Held per field in the crop's `sourceRefs` object, keyed by the field name it justifies. `note` quotes the published text and names the repo doc path.
rules.confidenceCodes: P = primary/government verified. S = secondary (verify before viva). Codes are the ones used by scoring-model.md's Conf column.
rules.urlsAsWritten: Source URLs are reproduced EXACTLY as the repo doc writes them, including bare domains without a scheme (e.g. 'nhb.gov.in'). No scheme, path or deep link was added. `url: null` means the doc names a source but publishes no URL for it.
rules.accessedSemantics: `accessed: 2026-08-13` is the date these values were read out of the repo docs. docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md records the underlying external research as a 'subagent report 2026-08-12'. The external pages themselves were NOT re-fetched for this file.
rules.soilVocabulary: The farm soilType enum is alluvial|black|red|laterite|sandy|loamy|clay|unknown (docs/database/schema.md). soilSuitability is populated ONLY from explicit numeric 0-3 scores in the source table.

gaps.field: soilSuitability — WHEAT, MAIZE, SOYBEAN, TOMATO, POTATO, ONION, CHILLI (7 of 9 crops)
gaps.problem: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md describes best soils in PROSE only, with no numeric 0-3 score for any soil: wheat 'well-drained loam/clay-loam, alluvial'; maize 'well-drained loam/alluvial'; soybean 'loam/black belt, well-drained'; tomato 'well-drained sandy loam + organics'; potato 'sandy loam, slightly acidic'; onion 'friable sandy loam–loam, humus'; chilli 'light fertile loam, pH 6–7'.
gaps.checked: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md (full table + Sources + open tasks), docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md, docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md, docs/database/schema.md, docs/irrigation/irrigation-model.md. No numeric soil-suitability score table exists anywhere in the repo.
gaps.impact: docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md defines a HARD GATE on 'soil suitability score 0' and weights S_soil at 0.25 of the total score. Neither can be evaluated for these 7 crops until scores are sourced.
gaps.resolution: Field OMITTED for all 7. Converting prose ('well-drained loam') into 0-3 scores across the 8-soil enum would be invention and was not done. A human agronomist or an ICAR/SAU soil-suitability source must author the scores.

gaps.field: soilSuitability — RICE (contradicts the assumption that cotton is the only scored crop)
gaps.problem: The rice row DOES publish one explicit numeric score: 'clay, clay-loam/alluvial (needs standing water) → sandy 0'. The column header is 'Best soils (score 3) → unsuitable (0)', which implies clay/clay-loam/alluvial are the 3s — but the row never writes the digit 3 against them, and 'clay-loam' is not a member of the farm soilType enum.
gaps.checked: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md line 7; soil enum in docs/database/schema.md.
gaps.impact: The single published fact 'sandy = 0' is a hard-gate value for rice under docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md and is currently NOT captured in the registry seed.
gaps.resolution: Field OMITTED entirely rather than partially populated with {sandy: 0}, per the transcription rule for this file. FLAGGED FOR THE REVIEWER: this is a real published score that a follow-up decision should capture — either seed {sandy: 0} alone, or have a human complete the full 8-soil row.

gaps.problem: Only black 3, alluvial 2 and red 1 are published. laterite, sandy, loamy, clay and unknown have no published score.
gaps.impact: An engine that treats 'absent' as 0 would hard-gate cotton out of loamy and clay soils with no source basis; one that treats absent as neutral would score it identically to a sourced value. The gate semantics for missing soils are not defined in docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md.
gaps.resolution: Only the 3 published scores are recorded. Missing-key semantics must be decided by a human and documented; do not default to 0.

gaps.problem: The Season cell publishes only the word 'Multi-season'. It does not name Kharif, Rabi or Zaid.
gaps.impact: docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md hard-gates on 'season ∉ crop's sowing windows for the state'. With seasons absent, tomato either never gates or always gates, depending on implementation.
gaps.resolution: Field OMITTED. NOTE THE CONFLICT: docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md's registry-shape example shows seasons: ["KHARIF","RABI"] — but that block is an illustrative document template (its comment reads '// per typical Indian calendar'), not a sourced agronomic claim, and it disagrees with 'Multi-season'. Needs a DES crop-calendar lookup and a human decision.

gaps.problem: Published as 'Kharif (+Rabi/spring)'. 'Spring maize' is a real Indian cropping window but the repo never states whether it maps to the ZAID enum member.
gaps.checked: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md line 9; searched the whole docs/ tree for 'Zaid' — it appears only as an enum/wizard option (docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md 'target season (Kharif/Rabi/Zaid)'), never assigned to a crop.
gaps.impact: Maize may be wrongly gated out of a Zaid recommendation request.
gaps.resolution: KHARIF and RABI transcribed; ZAID deliberately NOT asserted. A DES crop-calendar check should settle it.

gaps.problem: Published as '~24 vegetative, ~20 tuberisation' — two APPROXIMATE stage-specific point values, not a range. Reducing them to {min:20, max:24} would fabricate a range boundary the source never states, and would also silently discard the stage scoping and the '~' approximation markers.
gaps.checked: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md line 13; docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md registry shape (which has no stage-scoped temperature field).
gaps.impact: docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md's S_temp term (weight 0.15) cannot be computed for potato.
gaps.resolution: Field OMITTED. The verbatim string is preserved in POTATO.published.tempOptC. Either source a true potato optimum range (NHB PDF), or add a stage-scoped temperature field to the registry shape — the latter is a schema change requiring approval.

gaps.problem: Published as 'fruit set 15–20 (hot-set >20)'. 15–20 is a clean range and was transcribed, BUT the source scopes it to FRUIT SET, whereas docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md consumes tempOpt as a whole-season optimum ('S_temp = overlap of district seasonal normals with crop optimum range'). Indian tomato is widely grown where seasonal normals exceed 20 °C, so this value will score tomato harshly for a reason the source does not support.
gaps.impact: Systematic under-scoring of tomato in the crop recommendation engine; also the '(hot-set >20)' hot-set-variety note has nowhere to live in the registry shape.
gaps.resolution: Value transcribed as published with the scope recorded in sourceRefs.tempOpt.note and in this gap. A human must decide whether the engine may use a fruit-set optimum as a season optimum.

gaps.field: seasons — the ZAID enum member is unused
gaps.problem: No crop in the source table is assigned to Zaid. The wizard nonetheless offers Zaid as a target season.
gaps.impact: A Zaid recommendation request would gate out all 9 crops and return an empty ranked list.
gaps.resolution: Recorded as a knowledge gap, not patched. Either source Zaid crops from the DES crop calendar or handle the empty-result case explicitly in the engine.

gaps.problem: The source table publishes pH only twice: chilli 'pH 6–7' and potato 'slightly acidic' (qualitative). The tomato Conf cell carries an explicit instruction: 'pH conflict in sources — **do not quote pH**', and the doc's open tasks list 'Tomato pH via TNAU horticulture portal (until then: omitted)'.
gaps.checked: docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md lines 12-14 and the open-verification list.
gaps.impact: None for the current engine — docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md's registry shape defines no pH field.
gaps.resolution: No pH field created for any crop. The chilli 'pH 6–7' string is preserved verbatim in CHILLI.published.bestSoils so nothing is lost.

gaps.field: market.aliases — only 3 of 9 crops have real alias lists

gaps.impact: docs/market/data-normalization.md drops any row whose commodity string misses the alias map, and aborts the batch above a 30% drop rate. Single-string alias lists for six crops make that drop rate a live risk on first run — Agmarknet's real strings (e.g. bracketed variety suffixes as seen in 'Paddy(Dhan)(Common)') are exactly the naming inconsistency the doc warns about.
gaps.resolution: Only the written strings are transcribed. The real alias table must be built from an actual data.gov.in commodity listing before the first market job run; no alias was guessed.
